Messages.Author: Ankha
Messages.Body:
Name: Pin the Fly
Cardtype: Combat
Discipline: Potence
[pot] Only usable at the end of a round of combat in which this vampire successfully inflicted more damage at close range with a melee weapon than the opposing vampire. Not usable by a vampire being burned or going into torpor. Burn that melee weapon to put this card on the opposing vampire. The vampire with this card doesn't untap as normal. Any minion may burn this card as a +1 stealth action.
[POT] As above, and send that vampire into torpor.

A variation on Disarm. It costs an unbroken melee weapon (careful with that WWS) to immobilize a vampire. I didn't want it to do the "send to torpor" effect at
inferior to leave its utility to Disarm.

Thoughts? Comments?

Prince of Paris, France

Ratings Coordinator, Rules Director

Messages.Author: Ohlmann
Messages.Body:
I love the idea of helping melee weapon combat, it's currently pretty weak. Still, the cost is pretty high and this card can't be played too often. I would actually make a completely different inferior level that don't burn weapon and a superior level that do, maybe ?

Also, it's a pentex subvertion like effect : the vampire don't act until another minion rescue him. This mean also that the card is much more precious against big cap than against small cap.

As a variation on the idea, I would replace the superior level with 'burn the vampire at its controller minion phase' : the idea is that the vampire is pined to the sun and will burn if not rescued. May need another clause to avoid it being too overpowered (or be another card, more difficult to play)

Messages.Author: jamesatzephyr
Messages.Body:
> Ankha wrote:
> Role playing arguments are out of consideration. See Memory of Mortality on a Great Beast, a Sensory Deprived vampire that can wake etc.
>
Once a card is 'finished', they're out of consideration. The card does what the card does, even if it means a snake-formed-from-blood is running round on a Sport Bike with an elephant following.

However, it's perfectly possible to include role-playing arguments into the design of a card. If there's a note in Clanbook Gangrel, there's no reason not to put "This card costs Gangrel an additional blood" into some card text, or "Cannot be played by a Cardinal or Regent", or whatever. Similarly, you can rethink the implementation so that silly things don't happen - perhaps now it's a reaction, not a combat card, most of the allies-who-are-pseudo-vampires silliness doen't happen, or whatever else.

Obviously, you need to strike a balance - you don't want cards covered in lines and lines of 'fun' corner-cases. But a little perk or drawback here or there is great, and thinking about the role-playing implications of a card during design is totally legitimate. After all, if you can think of two alternative designs for a card, both are great cards, and one has more role-playing flavour, there's little reason not to pick it.

Messages.Author: Ohlmann
Messages.Body:
Well, Concelead work pretty well but need a combos and even if you have both part you need to enter combat in addition. That's why it jam hand easily.

I would see two way to help with that :

* an action that let you equip a weapon and in the same action rush / bleed someone. Kind of a bum's rush with "equip a weapon before combat" instead of "have a free maneuver". The blocked case is somewhat problematic (maybe "equip a weapon before any combat until the end of the action" ?). You still need the combos, but the equiping card is still useful without weapon and you don't need to enter combat in addition to have the combo

* a concealed that doesn't need you to have the weapon, like a vast wealth in combat card. Maybe something with the research area, I.E. you first play some card to fill the research area with melee weapon, and then you take card from it with another battle card.

Also, Angel of Berlin is a weapon support that work well and can be a third way for that.
